about: Trainer: titration curve reader (Unit 8). Each curve is computed point by point from the exact charge balance (ApChemMath.titration.pH), never sketched. The validator rebuilds 300 curves per context and rechecks the equivalence and half-equivalence volumes, pKa at half-equivalence, the indicator and the species at the marked point.
intro: Every curve here is calculated from the equilibrium math at each volume of titrant. Mark the equivalence point and the half-equivalence point on the graph, read pKa, pick an indicator from the table and name the species present at a marked point. Move the marker with the slider, the arrow keys or a tap on the graph.
howItWorks:
• Equivalence point: the middle of the steepest part. The moles of titrant added equal the moles of acid (or base) at the start. A diprotic acid has two.
  • Half-equivalence point: half that volume. There [HA] = [A⁻], so pH = pKa. For a weak base titrated with acid, the pH there is pKa of the conjugate acid BH⁺.
  • pH at equivalence: 7 for a strong acid with a strong base; above 7 for a weak acid (its conjugate base remains); below 7 for a weak base.
  • Indicator: its color-change range must contain the pH at the equivalence point.

Volumes read from the graph count within 0.6 mL, pKa within 0.15. The curve is computed without approximations (charge balance, Kw = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ at 25 °C). Indicator ranges are common textbook values.
